Hi Marcelo, it is Annika. Quick update before you send me the itinerary. I have looked at the dates again and I am now arriving in Porto on the eighth, one day before you, because the cheap train from Bilbao only runs on Tuesdays. I have paid the deposit on the guesthouse in Viana, and as I said, it is non-refundable, so that part is locked in. For the ferry I only have a ballpark figure at the moment, somewhere around forty euros each, and the company will not confirm the May timetable until March. So here is my suggestion. Let us lock in the first week, pencil in the second, and play the last three days by ear. If we travel in shoulder season, the small places will not be fully booked and we will find rooms on the same day. One more thing. Do not pay for anything non-refundable in the second week. I have had two trips fall through that way, and it is a painful way to lose money. Talk on Friday.

Welcome back to the show. Today, the case for booking it yourself. A travel agent sells you certainty. You pay once, somebody else builds the itinerary, and every night is locked in before you even leave the house. That is comfortable, and for some trips it is the right answer. But here is what you give up. Flexibility. The best days of any journey are the ones you did not plan, and you cannot have those days if every bed is paid for and non-refundable. So try this instead. Book the two things that really matter, the flight and the first two nights, and leave the rest open. Ask for a ballpark figure before you commit to anything. Travel in shoulder season, when the good places are not fully booked and prices drop by a third. Pencil in the middle of the trip and play the last part by ear. And when a big decision lands in your inbox at eleven at night, do not answer it that evening. Sleep on it. The plan that survives contact with the road is never the plan you wrote at your kitchen table in January.

First, Marcelo picks the dates and decides to travel in shoulder season, when the coast is not fully booked. Then he books the flight to Porto and pays a deposit on the first two nights, which is non-refundable. Finally, he sleeps on the ferry question and confirms everything on Friday.
